meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian interj meaning 'thank you', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Большое спасибо, папа, ты меня спас!
examples.trans: Thank you very much, Dad, you saved me!

поступить.gloss: to enter, to get into (a university); to act

meanings.en: to enter, to get into (a university); to act
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'ступить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to enter', forming an aspectual pair with 'поступать'.

examples.text: Герман, спасибо вам, вы поступили очень благородно!
examples.trans: German, thank you, you acted very nobly!

examples.text: Юле надо поступить в институт.
examples.trans: Yulia needs to get into university.

examples.text: Он поступил в институт.
examples.trans: He got into university.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.

examples.text: Знаешь, Денис, ты мне тоже очень нравишься.

examples.text: Он очень строгий и суровый человек.

examples.text: У меня аллергия на очень хорошую жизнь!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

examples.trans: Who is here? Why is it so quiet in the room?

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
